questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{-1/2},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{-1/2} & =1 \\ z & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=1$ is the surface $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡z$ that passes through the point $P(4,3,e).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4,3,e) & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡e=\sqrt{25}-1=4\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=4.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡z & =4 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡z \\ {e}^{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4} & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡z} \\ {e}^{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4} & =z\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(4,3,e)$ is the surface $z={e}^{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4}.$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y+{z}^{2}$ that passes through the point $P(1,0,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0,1) & =1\cdot {0}^{2}+{1}^{2}\cdot 0+{1}^{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y+{z}^{2} & =1 \\ z & =\pm \sqrt{1-x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,0,1)$ is the surface $z=\pm \sqrt{1-x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y}.$

questions.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}} & =c \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}} & ={c}^{2} \\ {c}^{2}{z}^{2}-{c}^{2}{x}^{2}-{c}^{2}{y}^{2} & =1 \\ {c}^{2}{x}^{2}+{c}^{2}{y}^{2}-{c}^{2}{z}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $f(x,y,z)$ can't be zero or negative. Therefore, we get a family of hyperboloids of two sheets:

$$
{c}^{2}{x}^{2}+{c}^{2}{y}^{2}-{c}^{2}{z}^{2}=-1,\,c\in (0,\infty ).
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-z+2?$
questions.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ {x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-z+2 & =c \\ z & ={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+2-c\end{aligned}
$$

If we let $2-c=C,$ we get a family of hyperbolic paraboloids:

$$
z={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+C,\,c\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
